dialogue.arabic: أهلين هادي، منيحة الحمد لله. وينك كنت مبارح؟
dialogue.transliteration: ahlein Hadi, mnii7a el-7amdulillah. weinak kent mbeeri7?
dialogue.english: Hi Hadi, good, thank God. Where were you yesterday?

dialogue.transliteration: kent besh-shughul, kaan 3indi dawaam la7add el-3ashiyye

dialogue.transliteration: la2, ma kaan fi wa2et. akalt bas bil-leil bil-beit
dialogue.english: No, there was no time. I only ate at night at home.

dialogue.transliteration: 2a3det 3and Saa7bti shwayy w-sherbna 2ahwe
dialogue.english: I sat at my friend's place a bit and we drank coffee.

lessons.culture: مبارح is the everyday Lebanese word for yesterday, and أول مبارح is the day before; the MSA أمس sounds like the news, not like a chat. Asking شو عملت مبارح؟ is a normal way to open a catch-up over coffee with a friend or neighbor.

exercises.tip: مبارح replaces the MSA أمس in everyday speech.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: شو يا ماريا، بتذكري لمّا كنا زغار؟
dialogue.transliteration: shu yaa Maria, bet-zakkeri lamma kenna zghaar?
dialogue.english: Hey Maria, do you remember when we were little?

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.arabic: أكيد! أنا كبرت بحيّ قديم ببيروت، وكنت حب العب برّا
dialogue.transliteration: akiid! ana kbiret b-7ayy 2adiim b-beirut, w-kent 7ebb il3ab barra
dialogue.english: Of course! I grew up in an old neighborhood in Beirut, and I loved to play outside.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: وأنا كان عندي صاحب اسمو جاد، كنا نلعب كورة بالزاروب
dialogue.transliteration: w-ana kaan 3indi Saa7eb ismo Jaad, kenna nil3ab kuura bez-zaaruub
dialogue.english: And I had a friend named Jad, we used to play soccer in the alley.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.arabic: ههه، وأنا أول بسكليت كان عندي كان أحمر
dialogue.transliteration: hehe, w-ana awwal biskliit kaan 3indi kaan a7mar
dialogue.english: Haha, and the first bike I had was red.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: كل صيف كنا نروح عند جدي عالضيعة
dialogue.transliteration: kell Seef kenna nrou7 3and jiddi 3aD-Day3a
dialogue.english: Every summer we used to go to my grandfather's in the village.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.arabic: يا سلام! وستّي كانت تحكيلنا قصص قبل ما ننام
dialogue.transliteration: yaa salaam! w-setti kenit ti7kiilna 2iSaS 2abel ma nnaam
dialogue.english: Lovely! And my grandmother used to tell us stories before sleeping.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: وكنت خايف كتير من العتمة وأنا زغير
dialogue.transliteration: w-kent khaayef ktiir men el-3atme w-ana zghiir
dialogue.english: And I was very afraid of the dark when I was little.

dialogue.transliteration: mish ma3quul! ana kamaan. w-kenna nemshi 3al-madrase sawa kell yoom
dialogue.english: No way! Me too. And we used to walk to school together every day.

dialogue.speaker: Karim

dialogue.transliteration: mou3allimti bil-madrase kenit ktiir 7anuune
dialogue.english: My teacher at school was very kind.

dialogue.transliteration: shu 7elwe hal-2ayyaam, allah yirja3ha
dialogue.english: How lovely those days were, may God bring them back.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.arabic: إي والله، وقتها كانت الدني أبسط بكتير
dialogue.transliteration: ee wallah, wa2ta kenit id-denye absaT b-ktiir

lessons.culture: Many Lebanese families spend the summer in the family's village (الضيعة) with the grandparents, and old Beirut neighborhoods are full of narrow alleys called زواريب where children played football. Talking about الأيام الحلوة, the good old days, is a favorite way to bond.

dialogue.english: Good morning Tarek, what's wrong? You look tired.

dialogue.arabic: لأ ما بصدّق، يمكن بس إشاعة
dialogue.transliteration: la2 ma baSaddi2, yimken bas 2ishaa3a
dialogue.english: No, I don't believe it, it might just be a rumor.

dialogue.speaker: Rita
dialogue.arabic: معك حق، لسّا مش متأكدين. وإختي تجوّزت الشهر اللي فات
dialogue.transliteration: ma3ak 7a2, lissa mish met2akkdiin. w-2ikhti tjawwazet esh-shahr illi faat
dialogue.english: You're right, we're not sure yet. And my sister got married last month.

dialogue.speaker: George
dialogue.arabic: مبروك! ما كنت أعرف. الله يخلّيلكن ياها
dialogue.transliteration: mabruuk! ma kent a3ref. allah yikhalliilkon yaaha
dialogue.english: Congratulations! I didn't know. God keep her for you.

dialogue.speaker: Rita
dialogue.arabic: الله يبارك فيك. وسمعنا إنّو جابوا صبي
dialogue.transliteration: allah ybaarek fiik. w-sme3na 2inno jaabu Sabi
dialogue.english: God bless you. And we heard they had a baby boy.

dialogue.speaker: George
dialogue.arabic: ألف مبروك! ما تقولي لحدا، بس سمعت إنّن رح يسافروا
dialogue.transliteration: alf mabruuk! ma t2uuli la-7ada, bas sme3et 2innon ra7 ysaafru
dialogue.english: A thousand congratulations! Don't tell anyone, but I heard they're going to travel.

dialogue.speaker: Rita
dialogue.arabic: هيدا كلّو حكي ناس، ما بعرف إذا صحيح ولّا لأ
dialogue.transliteration: heyda kello 7ki naas, ma ba3ref iza Sa7ii7 walla la2
dialogue.english: That's all people's talk, I don't know if it's true or not.

dialogue.speaker: George
dialogue.arabic: معك حق، خلينا ننتظر ونشوف
dialogue.transliteration: ma3ik 7a2, khaliina nentiZer w-nshuuf
dialogue.english: You're right, let's wait and see.

pair.english: Is it true that they're getting married?

response.english: I don't know, that's what they're saying.

lessons.culture: Neighbors and relatives in Lebanon share news constantly, and good news is met with مبروك or الله يتمّملو بالخير. Before repeating gossip people often protect themselves with عم يقولوا, they are saying, or ما بعرف إذا صحيح.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: "سمعت إنّو سامر خطب". Reply asking who told you this news.

too_formal.feedback: أخبرك is MSA; Lebanese say مين قلّك.

exercises.prompt: Someone says: "إختي تجوّزت الشهر اللي فات". Reply with congratulations.

too_formal.feedback: That blessing is correct but formal; مبروك is what is said first.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "_____ إنّو محلّ فلان سكّر." Meaning: They're saying that such-and-such shop closed.

too_formal.feedback: يقال is bookish; Lebanese say عم يقولوا.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "لسّا مش متأكدين، يمكن بس _____." Meaning: We're not sure yet, it might just be a rumor.

too_formal.feedback: شائعة is MSA spelling and sound; Lebanese say إشاعة.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "What's the latest news with you?"

too_formal.feedback: آخر أخبارك is formal; شو الجديد is what people ask.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "You won't believe what happened yesterday in the neighborhood."
exercises.answer: ما رح تصدّق شو صار مبارح بالحيّ
accepted: ما رح تصدّق شو صار مبارح بالحيّ
ma ra7 teSSaddi2 shu Saar mbeeri7 bil-7ayy
ما رح تصدق شو صار مبارح بالحي

too_formal.item: لن تصدق ما حدث أمس في الحي
too_formal.feedback: لن and ما حدث are MSA; Lebanese say ما رح and شو صار.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "They told me you're moving to a new house"?
options: قالولي إنّك عم تنقل ع بيت جديد
exercises.answer: قالولي إنّك عم تنقل ع بيت جديد
accepted: قالولي إنّك عم تنقل ع بيت جديد

too_formal.item: أخبروني أنك تنتقل إلى منزل جديد
too_formal.feedback: أخبروني and منزل are formal; say قالولي and بيت.

exercises.prompt: How do you say "a baby boy" in Lebanese?

too_formal.feedback: ولد ذكر is formal; Lebanese say صبي.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: I heard that Samer got engaged.

too_formal.feedback: أن is formal; Lebanese say إنّو.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: That's all just people's talk.

too_formal.feedback: هذا and كلام are MSA; Lebanese say هيدا and حكي.

challenge.title: Tell Me What Happened
challenge.instructions: Write and say a short Lebanese conversation of at least 10 lines between two people catching up. It must include asking what happened yesterday, an answer in the past tense, a childhood memory, one thing that went wrong, and one piece of news or gossip you heard. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 16 and include both a masculine-address form and a feminine-address form.
required_elements: A question about yesterday using مبارح and شو عملت or شو صار.
An answer describing something that happened, using a past-tense verb.
A memory from childhood using لمّا كنت زغير or كنّا.
Something that went wrong, using a word like خرب, ضيّعت, or تأخّرت.
A piece of news or gossip introduced with سمعت إنّو or قالولي.
At least one masculine-address form such as كنت or شفت.
At least one feminine-address form such as كنتي or شفتي.
A closing reaction such as يي, يا حرام, or الله يعينك.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: ميساء، كيفك؟ شو عملتي مبارح؟
dialogue.transliteration: Maysaa2, kiifik? shu 3milti mbeeri7?
dialogue.english: Maysa, how are you? What did you do yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Maysaa
dialogue.arabic: أهلين بلال، ما رح تصدّق شو صار معي مبارح!
dialogue.transliteration: ahlein Bilaal, ma ra7 teSSaddi2 shu Saar ma3i mbeeri7!
dialogue.english: Hi Bilal, you won't believe what happened to me yesterday!

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: شو في؟ قوليلي!
dialogue.transliteration: shu fii? 2uuliili!
dialogue.english: What is it? Tell me!

dialogue.speaker: Maysaa
dialogue.arabic: تلفوني خرب وضيّعت مفتاح البيت بنفس اليوم
dialogue.transliteration: talifuuni khirib w-Dayya3et miftaa7 el-beit b-nafs el-yoom
dialogue.english: My phone broke and I lost the house key on the same day.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: يي، يا حرام! هيك يوم بيذكّرني لمّا كنت زغير، كنا نضيّع كل شي!
dialogue.transliteration: yii, yaa 7araam! heik yoom bizakkerni lamma kent zghiir, kenna nDayyi3 kell shi!
dialogue.english: Oh no! A day like that reminds me of when I was little, we used to lose everything!

dialogue.speaker: Maysaa
dialogue.arabic: ههه صحيح! بس بالآخر لقيت المفتاح
dialogue.transliteration: hehe Sa7ii7! bas bil-aakher la2eit el-miftaa7
dialogue.english: Haha true! But in the end I found the key.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله. بالمناسبة، سمعت إنّو سامر خطب
dialogue.transliteration: el-7amdulillah. bel-munaasabe, sme3et 2inno Saamer khaTab
dialogue.english: Thank God. By the way, I heard Samer got engaged.

dialogue.speaker: Maysaa
dialogue.arabic: عن جدّ؟ مين قلّك؟ ما كنت أعرف!
dialogue.transliteration: 3an jadd? meen 2allak? ma kent a3ref!
dialogue.english: Really? Who told you? I didn't know!

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: قالولي الجيران، بس لسّا مش متأكد إذا صحيح
dialogue.transliteration: 2aaloolli el-jiiraan, bas lissa mish met2akked iza Sa7ii7
dialogue.english: The neighbors told me, but I'm not sure yet if it's true.

dialogue.speaker: Maysaa
dialogue.arabic: ما بعرف، عم يقولوا هيك. خلينا ننتظر ونشوف
dialogue.transliteration: ma ba3ref, 3am ye2uulu heik. khaliina nentiZer w-nshuuf
dialogue.english: I don't know, that's what they're saying. Let's wait and see.
